old_caption: The video opens with a dark, atmospheric scene featuring a series of illuminated structures that resemble futuristic vehicles or spacecraft. These structures are adorned with bright lights, predominantly white and orange, which create a striking contrast against the dark background. The camera pans slowly from left to right, revealing more of these glowing objects as they appear to be moving or floating in a vast, dark space. As the camera continues its movement, it captures the dynamic interplay of light and shadow, enhancing the sense of depth and mystery. The scene is enveloped in a misty haze, adding an ethereal quality to the environment. The overall ambiance is one of intrigue and anticipation, suggesting a setting that could be part of a science fiction narrative or a high-tech event.

caption: A dark stage lighting rig fills a side-by-side stereo fisheye view, its left and right halves mirroring one another across pure black. Symmetric overhead trusses carry bright white LED strips and rows of round orange dots, while a diagonal arm of orange dots hangs from each top corner. Across the early frames these orange dots steadily saturate and the corner arms lengthen toward the center, as the small outlined fixture clusters low in each half brighten in place. Volumetric white beams then emerge from the upper moving-head fixtures, angling downward and inward. The beams intensify until they cross near the center in an X, and a crowd of tiny white human silhouettes along the bottom edge becomes progressively lit. The sequence holds its mirrored geometry throughout.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.

timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
